chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'The black, beastly dog, its game is not edible, because the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) commanded to kill it.'
ai.seo_question: Why is the game of the black dog not considered halal according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between general hunting dogs and the specific 'black, beastly dog' (al-kalb al-aswad al-bahim), whose game is deemed inedible due to the Prophet's command to kill it. In Shia jurisprudence, this highlights the principle that not all dogs are ritually impure or disqualified from hunting, but specific types or conditions may render their catch impermissible based on prophetic precedent.

en.sarwar: 20. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ’Amir al-Mu’minin has said, ‘

What a very black colored dog hunts is not edible because the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, commanded to kill it.’”
